newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Sept 2.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Sept 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The St George game plan for its grand final match against Manly will be one of running at Manly's defence, rather than running the ball wide. Mark Coyne and Nathan Brown said yesterday that St George will need a minimum of three tries to beat Manly. Page 36.

North Melbourne coach Denis Pagan isolated Stuart Anderson from the rest of the team after a 50-minute training session yesterday to see if he was fully recovered from a hamstring injury. Pagan said Anderson probably could have played last week, but he wnted to make sure he was fully fit for the AFL grand final. Page 36.

Manly coach Bob Fulton has sought reassurance from referees' coordinator Mick Stone that his players Matthew Ridge and Geoff Toovey will have complete protection in Sunday's rugby league grand final as they may be targets for St George players as they both are suffering from injuries. Page 34.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD
St George coach David Waite, amid speculation that many St George players want now to stay with the club, has told his players to honour their contracts to rival clubs next season. Page 40.

Eastwood's premiership is in doubt after the Australian Rugby Football Union told them that fullback Matt Burke should not play in tomorrow night's preliminary final due to injuries he has sustained. Page 39.

Eastern Suburbs second rower Rob Johnston could be wearing a Queensland jersey by November on an extensive rugby union tour of Great Britain. Queensland coach John Connolly yesterday stated that he was confident Johnston would play for the Reds next season. Page 39.
THE AGE

The AFL yesterday said that Sydney chairman Richard Colless' raising of an incident involving North Melbourne's Wayne Carey was ill-considered and out of line, stating that he should know better than to raise an issue through the media. Page C8.
Footscray could lose Chris Grant to Port Power in a new AFL player deal. Grant is already believed to be close to signing a three-year A$1.5 million contract with Port Power. Page C8.

Collingwood president Kevin Rose has blamed the AFL's slow reaction to the Andrew Dunkley affair for the reason the Supreme Court has ruled that Dunkley can play in Saturday's grand final, even with a striking charge against him. Page C8.
HERALD SUN

The Sydney Swans have won the first unofficial points of the AFL grand final in their Supreme Court win clearing Andrew Dunkley to play in tomorrow's big game. The court granted Dunkley a court injunction until next Tuesday. Page 1.

Todd Viney, Melbourne's midfielder who was recruited in 1987 from Adelaide, is seen as one of the key players on Port Power's shopping list. Melbourne's football manager Richard Griffiths confirmed yesterday the South Australian interest in Viney. Page 11.

North Melbourne ruck forward Corey McKernan has put critics off his knee injury by putting in a brisk training session yesterday, kicking a 45-metre goal that sparked the applause of 5000 fans who were watching. Page 108.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The AFL Centenary looks destined to end in controversy after yesterday's Supreme Court decision to postpone hearings against Andrew Dunkley until Tuesday next week, after the grand final is over. Page 120.

Nova Peris, one of Australia's gold medal-winning hockey players, will make a daring career move from hockey to the track. She will move from Darwin to Sydney to start training for her ambition to be a sprinter. Page 118.

If everything goes according to plan, jockey Darren Beadman will be riding Saintly and not Octagonal in the A$1.5 million W S Cox Plate next week. Octagonal made a great comeback at last Sunday's A$200,000 Group 1 Underwood Stakes at Caulfield, making Beaman's decision much awaited. Page 118.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
